items.title: Saved-search export MVP
items.outcome: Pilot customers can take their saved search data with them.
acceptanceCriteria: The required export capability works end to end for pilot customers.
verification: Record a pilot acceptance session with a successful downloaded export.

items.title: Download saved searches as CSV
items.outcome: An authenticated customer can download their own saved searches in the agreed CSV format.
acceptanceCriteria: The pilot environment provides a documented export action producing only the requesting customer's data.
verification: Exercise the deployed action with pilot accounts and inspect output and access isolation.

items.title: Export my saved searches without exposing another customer's data
items.outcome: A customer obtains a valid file containing exactly their own saved searches, including an empty collection.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with saved searches, the download contains those rows in the agreed format.
Given an empty collection, the download contains headers and no data rows.
A customer cannot export another customer's saved searches.
verification: Run end-to-end cases for populated, empty, and unauthorized cross-account requests.

items.title: Define the CSV contract and examples
items.outcome: An agreed contract defines columns, escaping, encoding, and empty-file behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: The contract includes sample populated and empty exports and escaping examples.
verification: Review fixtures against the agreed consumer requirements and record the decision.

items.title: Implement and verify the authenticated CSV download

dependencyReasons.format-task: The download implementation consumes the agreed CSV columns, encoding, and fixtures.

items.outcome: The export action emits contract-compliant CSV for the requesting account.
acceptanceCriteria: Populated, empty, escaped-value, and unauthorized requests match the agreed behavior.
verification: Run contract and access-isolation tests and inspect an actual downloaded file.

items.title: Fix the existing login crash after session expiry
items.outcome: The existing login flow handles an expired session without crashing.
items.expectedBehavior: The established session-expiry contract returns the customer to sign-in.
items.observedBehavior: The current flow crashes after an expired session is submitted.
acceptanceCriteria: An expired session returns to sign-in without an unhandled error.
verification: Reproduce the expired-session case and add/run a regression check for the established behavior.
